issue.title: Fade the global bypass the right way round
issue.body:
make_one_noise() walks 'disable' towards 'disable_all' one sample at a time so that switching bypass is a 100ms crossfade, and passes single_sample() disable / EFF_ENABLE_STEPS as the mix.  But single_sample() takes its mix the other way up: 1.0 is the processed signal and 0.0 the untouched input, which is what bypass() passes.  So the ramp runs backwards.

Engaging bypass cuts straight to the dry input, fades the effects back in over 100ms, and then cuts to dry again once bypass() takes over. Releasing it is the mirror image.  Two steps per footswitch tap, with a tenth of a second of the wrong signal between them.

Nothing in Validation/ sees it, because the bench calls single_sample(1.0f) directly and never goes through the ramp.  Driving the real make_one_noise() on the host instead, with Test Tone routed and silence on the input, the tone's level in 5ms windows after a tap is

	before:  1.00 1.00 0.89 0.10 0.15 0.19 ... 0.94 1.00 0.89 0.00
	after:   1.00 1.00 0.99 0.95 0.90 0.84 ... 0.09 0.05 0.00

comment.body: D'oh. Pulled. I hardly ever test with bypass on, and I don't do it while there's any playing going on.
